note: Where to get footage, stills and sound you are allowed to use. Cutright does not download anything and does not host anything — this is a directory, so the agent can point you at the right place and tell you what the licence asks of you before you commit to a clip.

cc0.name: CC0 / public domain
cc0.plain: Do what you like. No credit needed.

cc-by.name: CC BY
cc-by.plain: Free to use commercially, but you MUST credit the creator.

cc-by-sa.name: CC BY-SA
cc-by-sa.plain: Credit required, and anything you build from it carries the same licence. Read this one before using it in a client video.

cc-by-nc.name: CC BY-NC
cc-by-nc.plain: NOT for commercial use. A monetised video counts as commercial.

pexels.name: Pexels License
pexels.plain: Free for commercial use, no credit required. You may not sell the file itself, or imply the people in it endorse you.

unsplash.name: Unsplash License
unsplash.plain: Free for commercial use, no credit required. You may not build a competing stock service from it.

pixabay.name: Pixabay Content License
pixabay.plain: Free for commercial use, no credit required. You may not redistribute the file as-is on another stock site.

mixkit.name: Mixkit License
mixkit.plain: Free for commercial use, no credit required. Music and SFX have their own terms — read them for paid work.

mixed.name: Varies per item
mixed.plain: Every item carries its OWN licence. You have to read the one on the item, not the one on the site.

non-commercial-site.name: Personal / educational use only
non-commercial-site.plain: The site's own terms rule out commercial use. Not for a monetised or client video.

sources.name: Pexels Video
sources.good: Modern, well-lit b-roll. The safest default for commercial work.
sources.watch: Search results are heavily weighted to a few popular clips — the same beach shot is in a lot of videos.

sources.name: Pixabay Video
sources.good: One licence across footage, stills, music and effects, and no attribution to track.
sources.watch: Quality is uneven — plenty of it is upscaled or over-compressed. Check at full size before you commit.

sources.name: Mixkit
sources.good: Curated rather than crowd-sourced, so the hit rate is high. Good stingers and UI sounds.
sources.watch: The music and SFX licence differs from the video one. Read it for anything paid.

sources.name: Coverr
sources.good: Backgrounds and loops meant to sit behind text — which is most of what a tutorial needs.
sources.watch: Terms have changed more than once. Check the licence shown on the clip you are taking.

sources.name: NASA Image and Video Library
sources.good: Genuinely public domain, high resolution, and unlike anything on a stock site.
sources.watch: The NASA logo and identifiable people are NOT covered — you may not imply NASA endorses you.

sources.name: Internet Archive
sources.good: Archive footage, old film, radio. Nothing else has this depth.
sources.watch: Uploads are user-submitted and the stated licence is often wrong. Treat it as a lead, not a clearance.

sources.name: Unsplash
sources.good: The best-looking free photography on the web, and safe commercially.
sources.watch: Recognisable brands, logos and people appear constantly — that is a release problem, not a licence one.

sources.name: Openverse
sources.good: Searches many CC libraries at once and shows each item's licence up front.
sources.watch: It indexes CC BY-NC too. Filter to commercial use or you will pick something you cannot ship.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons
sources.good: Maps, diagrams, historical images and portraits you will not find elsewhere.
sources.watch: Mostly CC BY-SA — the share-alike clause can follow your video. Check before using it in client work.

sources.name: The Met — Open Access
sources.good: Half a million CC0 artworks at very high resolution.
sources.watch: Only items marked Open Access. The rest of the collection is not.

sources.name: Smithsonian Open Access
sources.good: Millions of CC0 items with real metadata attached.
sources.watch: The API key is free but required.

sources.name: Freesound
sources.good: The deepest library of real recorded sound effects there is.
sources.watch: Every sound has its own licence and plenty are CC BY-NC. Filter, and record the credit at the moment you download it — going back later is miserable.

sources.name: Free Music Archive
sources.good: Real music by real artists rather than production loops.
sources.watch: Per-track licences, many requiring credit and some barring commercial use.

sources.name: Musopen
sources.good: Public-domain classical, including recordings — not just scores.
sources.watch: The composition being public domain does not make the RECORDING public domain. Check the recording's own licence.

sources.name: Incompetech (Kevin MacLeod)
sources.good: Enormous, consistent, and genuinely usable commercially — if you credit it.
sources.watch: CC BY means the credit is mandatory, in the description. A paid licence removes that requirement.

sources.name: BBC Sound Effects
sources.good: Sixteen thousand archive effects, beautifully catalogued.
sources.watch: Personal, educational and research use ONLY under the RemArc licence. Not for a monetised video.
